newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Tallinna rebounds on Estonian bourse, gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Tallinna rebounds on Estonian bourse, gains seen.

text.p: Tallinna Bank gained the most on Estonia's market on Friday after its price fell sharply in early trade in response to a newspaper report that it faced a liquidity crunch earlier in the week, dealers said.
Overall market volume was 37.7 million kroons compared to 39.8 million kroons the previous session and the TALSE index lost 0.67 points to close at 253.40.
Tallinna Bank gained 2.05 kroons to close at 62.05 kroons in trade of 7.6 million kroons.
"The newspaper report did not mean much and so the price started to rise again," one dealer said, adding that the stock had fallen too far.
The Rakvere meat factory saw active trade for the third day in trade of 1.7 million kroons, but its closing price fell 0.12 kroons to close at 16.00 kroons.
Dealers said the stock was good and has potential to rise.

But the Tallinn bourse said late on Thursday that it would investigate the possibility that some investors might have had insider information on the company's acquisition of a meat plant in neighbouring Latvia.
The plant's price rose rapidly in high demand ahead of the announcement of the acquisition on Thursday.
Hansabank fell 1.99 kroons to close at 131.71 kroons and Forekspank fell 1.00 kroons to close at 178.80 kroons.
Dealers said prices are low and might attract more buyers next week.
